"Score the card 1-5 on each criterion. For each score give ref, the card line (card:<field>) that decides it, or plan:<field path> when no card line carries it, and a reason of at most 25 words. Use NA only where a criterion allows it. Then name decides_by: the id of the earliest phase after which decision_rule can be applied whichever outcome occurs, or \"none\". A phase that only reproduces a published number, or only measures throughput the question does not ask about, does not count. Give decides_by_reason in at most 25 words. Decide only from the text below; do not use tools.
Root question: generative pipeline for discovery of single phase immersion coolants
Option record: {\"id\":\"IC-V3\",\"title\":\"MD verification inserted into Org-Mol's ester shortlist before synthesis\",\"summary\":\"Data-centre immersion cooling needs dielectric liquids with low viscosity, high thermal conductivity and heat capacity, and PFAS rules are pushing the field towards PFAS-free esters. Restrict the generative search to synthetically accessible PFAS-free esters of the kind already ML-screened at scale, filter to a ranked shortlist, and MD-verify the top 100, 300 then 1000 candidates' viscosity and thermal conductivity before any synthesis decision. Score against measured data for known esters and commercial single-phase fluids held out of training, never against the predictors. More compute buys more MD-verified candidates and longer simulations per candidate, testing whether the best cooling figure of merit keeps climbing beyond the 461-candidate shortlist stage.\",\"root_link\":\"SAME: ester discovery kept on transport properties and on the down-selection step where prior work stops.\",\"compute_open\":\"MD-verified candidates (100–1000, anchored to a ~461-candidate shortlist) and simulation length per candidate. Unknown: whether MD meaningfully reorders an ML shortlist or merely confirms it.\",\"sequential\":\"not given\",\"source_urls\":[]}
Card:
card:question: Does molecular-dynamics verification of viscosity and thermal conductivity reorder a machine-learning ester shortlist, or merely confirm it, and does the best coolant keep improving?
card:hypothesis: Molecular dynamics will reorder the shortlist because the machine-learning viscosity error (22.5% MAPE) exceeds MD's, so better esters appear only after verification.
card:sequential_part: Each candidate's viscosity waits on one long trajectory; the ranking waits on 100, 300, then 1000 candidates.
card:method: Run each candidate as parallel short replicas on separate GPUs and block-average the Green-Kubo integrals, so wall-clock shrinks by the replica count.
card:if_lever: By 100 candidates the replica ranking matches the sequential baseline and diverges from ML; the best figure keeps improving through 1000.
card:if_not: Replicas only match the sequential baseline by 300 candidates, and MD then merely confirms the ML ranking, unchanged from 100 through 1000.
card:test_summary: Rent an 8-GPU A100 node; run OPLS-AA Green-Kubo viscosity and thermal conductivity for the top 100 then 300 of Org-Mol's 461 monoesters; compare ML-vs-MD rank correlation and whether the best cooling figure keeps climbing; time a 45 ns single-trajectory baseline against parallel 5 ns replicas.
card:closest_prior: Org-Mol screened 461 monoester cooling candidates with a transformer and measured only two by synthesis; none were molecular-dynamics-verified for viscosity or thermal conductivity [s1].
card:left_open: No published work runs Green-Kubo viscosity and thermal conductivity over a 100-to-1000 candidate ester shortlist, so whether MD reorders the ML ranking is untested.
card:anchor: Green-Kubo MD (OPLS-AA) reproduces Org-Mol Ester 1's measured 40 C viscosity 6.41 cSt
card:limits: Shows single-phase ranking only, under one force field and 15 ns sampling; no synthesis, dielectric, flammability, compatibility, or stability checks.

Criteria:
stakes: Take the two outcomes this test predicts, as measured here and within the limits in scope_gap. 5 = whichever occurs, a choice someone faces (what to buy, build, collect or scale next) changes, and the test measures the quantity that choice depends on; 3 = the outcomes bear on that choice only through a step this test does not check (a stand-in system, simulation to reality, a single model), or one outcome is already much more likely than the other; 1 = neither outcome would change anything. Do not score how famous the field is or how close it is to the root question.
lever: Could the result tell if_lever from if_not, with compute the only thing that changed? Check four conditions: (a) the predicted difference between if_lever and if_not is larger than what noise_rule says run-to-run noise can produce; (b) compute_axis spans at least 10×; (c) the varied quantity is bought with compute, not with more data, labels or people (when restructuring.method is not none: the arms run on the same hardware and differ only in method); (d) inputs that could also explain the difference are in held_fixed. 5 = all four hold; 3 = one fails or cannot be told from the plan; 1 = two or more fail, or the measured quantity is not the one the question asks about.
verifiable: What is the measured outcome scored against? 5 = an exact or planted truth that does not come from the method under test (a simulation's hidden true run, an exact success flag, a formal checker, planted items), and the setup first reproduces a published number within a stated tolerance; 3 = labels from a model or human rater with an agreement check, or exact truth with no reproduction step; 1 = nothing independent of the method's own output.
open: Does the closest published result already answer this question over this range? 5 = the quoted prior stops short of this range or asks a different question, and the plan states the gap; 3 = the prior answers part of it (a narrower range, a related system), or no prior is named; 1 = the quoted prior already answers it. Reusing published tools, models or benchmarks does not lower this score.
